hypotheses.statement: The concurrency increase from 8 to 32 workers caused database connection pool exhaustion because pool size (20) was insufficient for the increased worker count.
The service token expiry caused authentication failures to flags.internal, preventing workers from reading the settlement_v2_enabled flag and causing failures on approximately 31% of attempts.
The two faults (pool exhaustion and token expiry) were independent and coincidental, occurring four minutes apart, with combined effect explaining the 61% failure rate.
The failure ratio reduction from 0.61 to 0.29 after pool fix indicates pool exhaustion accounted for approximately 32% of failures (0.61 - 0.29).
The failure ratio reduction from 0.29 to 0.004 after token replacement indicates token expiry accounted for approximately 28.6% of failures (0.29 - 0.004).

observed_facts.statement: Configuration change at 15:55:00Z raised settlement-worker concurrency from 8 to 32 workers while database connection pool size remained at 20.
Database connection pool exhausted from 15:58:10Z with pool size 20, checked-out 20, queue depth rising, causing pool_timeout errors after 5000ms affecting approximately 0.38 of attempts.
Service token for flags.internal expired at 15:59:00Z on 2026-02-11 after 90 days, issued on 2025-11-13, with renewal not automated.
Calls to flags.internal returning 401 invalid_token from 15:59:02Z, causing worker to fail closed when unable to read settlement_v2_enabled flag, affecting approximately 0.31 of attempts.
Settlement failure ratio reached 0.61 against objective of 0.02, triggering alert at 16:00:44Z that did not clear until 18:12:30Z.
Connection pool raised to 64 at 17:20:15Z, stopping pool_timeout errors and reducing settlement failure ratio from 0.61 to 0.29.
Replacement token for flags.internal installed at 18:12:10Z, stopping 401 responses and reducing settlement failure ratio from 0.29 to 0.004.
The pool exhaustion and token expiry started four minutes apart and neither explains the other.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Configuration design documentation or architecture decision records explaining the relationship between worker concurrency and connection pool sizing.
open_questions.question: Why is database connection pool size not derived from worker concurrency to prevent such mismatches?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Inventory of service tokens with their issuance dates, expiry dates, and renewal automation status.
open_questions.question: Which other service tokens are on manual renewal and may be at risk of similar expiry?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Financial impact assessment or transaction volume data showing monetary exposure.
open_questions.question: What was the actual settlement value at risk during the incident?

summary: Payment settlement failures occurred due to two independent, coincidental faults: 1) Database connection pool exhaustion caused by a concurrency increase from 8 to 32 workers while pool size remained at 20, and 2) Service token expiry for flags.internal causing authentication failures. The combined effect resulted in a 61% failure rate. The pool issue accounted for approximately 32% of failures and was resolved by increasing pool size to 64. The token issue accounted for approximately 28.6% of failures and was resolved by token replacement.

timeline.statement: pool enlarged, failures reduced but not resolved
responder expects full recovery after pool fix
